words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: मुञ्चातक वात और पित्त को हरने वाला, मधुर और परम वृष्य है; वह जीवन देने वाला, बृंहण, वृष्य, कण्ठ के लिए हितकर और रसायन में प्रशस्त है।
english: Muñcātaka removes Vāta and Pitta, is sweet and supremely aphrodisiac; it is vitalizing, nourishing, aphrodisiac, good for the throat and recommended in rejuvenation (rasāyana).
notes: param is read with vṛṣyaḥ ('supremely aphrodisiac'); it could also stand alone ('excellent'). vṛṣya is printed twice, as given. muñcātaka is kept as printed, no identification.
lines_deva: जीवनो बृंहणो वृष्यः कण्ठ्यः शस्तो रसायने
lines_iast: jīvano bṛṃhaṇo vṛṣyaḥ kaṇṭhyaḥ śasto rasāyane

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: विदारी का कन्द बलकारक, मूत्रल, मधुर और शीतल है। अम्लिका का कन्द ग्रहणी और अर्श में हितकर और लघु माना गया है;
english: The tuber of vidārī is strengthening, diuretic, sweet and cold. The tuber of amlikā is held to be beneficial in grahaṇī and arśas, and light;
notes: SENTENCE: the description of the amlikā tuber continues into 122a. vidārī and amlikā are kept Sanskrit, no identification; grahaṇī and arśas kept Sanskrit.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: वह बहुत उष्ण नहीं, कफ और वात का नाशक, ग्राही और मदात्यय में प्रशस्त है। सार्षप शाक त्रिदोषकारक और मल-मूत्र को बाँधने वाला कहा जाता है।
english: It is not too hot, destroys Kapha and Vāta, is binding and recommended in madātyaya. The pot-herb (śāka) of sarṣapa is said to cause the three doṣas and to keep faeces and urine bound.
notes: SENTENCE: line a completes the amlikā tuber of 121b. Line c is printed inside round brackets (with its '|' inside the bracket): the edition's bracketed alternative, split as printed, glossed '(variant:)' and left out of the translations; its sense is 'Likewise would be (the pot-herb) of raktanāla, especially dry and sour.' tridoṣa is read as a bahuvrīhi 'causing (vitiating) the three doṣas'. sarṣapa = mustard (standard). raktanāla kept Sanskrit (literally 'red-stalk'), no identification; its gender is not shown by the genitive. madātyaya kept Sanskrit.

hindi: वैसे ही पिण्डालुक को जानना चाहिए, और कन्द होने के कारण वह मुख को प्रिय है। परन्तु सर्पच्छत्रक को छोड़कर छत्र की अन्य बहुत-सी जातियाँ
english: Likewise one should know piṇḍāluka; and because it is a tuber, it is pleasing to the mouth. But the many other kinds of mushroom (chatra), excluding the sarpacchatraka,

text_flags.why: bahvayaḥ is no form of bahu: the f. nom. pl. is bahvyaḥ (as gurvyaḥ, printed gurvya, in 124a); with bahvayo the pāda has 9 syllables, with bahvyo the required 8 (bah vyo 'nyāś cha tra jā ta yaḥ: syllables 5-7 tra jā ta = ⏑ – ⏑, as an even pāda requires)

notes: SENTENCE: line b runs into 124a. tadvat compares piṇḍāluka with an item before it; the text does not say which (the sārṣapa pot-herb of 122b, or raktanāla of the bracketed 122c). chatra = mushroom is the plain sense of the word; sarpacchatraka is literally 'snake-mushroom', no identification. piṇḍāluka kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: based on leaves, tubers and fruits
words.gram: m. nom. sg., bahuvrīhi (dvandva first members)

hindi: शीतल, पीनस उत्पन्न करने वाली, मधुर और गुरु ही हैं। यह पत्र, कन्द और फल पर आश्रित चौथा शाकवर्ग है।
english: are cold, cause pīnasa, and are sweet and indeed heavy. This is the fourth group, that of pot-herbs (śākavarga), based on leaves, tubers and fruits.
notes: SENTENCE: line a completes the mushrooms of 123b. Line b closes the group (verbless). pīnasa kept Sanskrit.
lines_deva: शीताः पीनसकर्त्र्यश्च मधुरा गुर्व्य एव च
lines_iast: śītāḥ pīnasakartryaśca madhurā gurvya eva ca

words.gloss: thirst, burning, fever, dyspnoea, raktapitta, kṣata and kṣaya

hindi: अब फलवर्ग — तृष्णा, दाह, ज्वर, श्वास, रक्तपित्त, क्षत और क्षय, वात-पित्त, उदावर्त, स्वरभेद, मदात्यय,
english: Now the group of fruits (phalavarga): thirst, burning, fever, dyspnoea, raktapitta, kṣata (wound) and kṣaya (wasting), Vāta-Pitta, udāvarta, hoarseness (svarabheda), madātyaya,
notes: 'atha phalavargaḥ---' is a prose heading typed at the head of the verse line; without it the line has 16 syllables. SENTENCE: these objects run into 126 (verb vyapohati, subject mṛdvīkā). raktapitta, udāvarta, madātyaya kept Sanskrit; kṣata and kṣaya kept with literal glosses.

hindi: मुख की तिक्तता, मुख का शोष और कास — इन्हें मृद्वीका शीघ्र दूर करती है; वह बृंहण, वृष्य, मधुर, स्निग्ध और शीतल है।
english: bitterness of the mouth, dryness of the mouth and cough, mṛdvīkā quickly removes; it is nourishing, aphrodisiac, sweet, unctuous and cold.
notes: SENTENCE: completes the list of 125. tiktāsyatā: 'the state of having a bitter mouth'. mṛdvīkā = grape (standard).

hindi: खर्जूर मधुर, बृंहण, वृष्य, गुरु और शीतल है; क्षय, अभिघात, दाह और वात-पित्त में वह हितकर है।
english: Kharjūra is sweet, nourishing, aphrodisiac, heavy and cold; it is beneficial in kṣaya, injury (abhighāta), burning and Vāta-Pitta.
notes: kharjūra = date (standard).
lines_deva: मधुरं बृंहणं वृष्यं खर्जूरं गुरु शीतलम्
क्षयेऽभिघाते दाहे च वातपित्ते च तद्धितम्
lines_iast: madhuraṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ kharjūraṃ guru śītalam
kṣaye'bhighāte dāhe ca vātapitte ca taddhitam

hindi: फल्गु, परूषक और मधूक तर्पण, बृंहण, गुरु, विष्टम्भी और शीतल हैं, और वात-पित्त में प्रशस्त हैं।
english: Phalgu, parūṣaka and madhūka are replenishing (tarpaṇa), nourishing, heavy, obstructive and cold, and are recommended in Vāta-Pitta.
notes: The qualities of line a are read as shared by phalgu, parūṣaka and madhūka (the singular śasyate going with each); alternatively line a describes phalgu alone and line b says only that parūṣaka and madhūka are recommended in Vāta-Pitta. viṣṭambhin = causing obstruction. phalgu, parūṣaka, madhūka kept Sanskrit, no identifications.
lines_deva: तर्पणं बृंहणं फल्गु गुरु विष्टम्भि शीतलम्
परूषकं मधूकं च वातपित्ते च शस्यते
lines_iast: tarpaṇaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ phalgu guru viṣṭambhi śītalam
parūṣakaṃ madhūkaṃ ca vātapitte ca śasyate

hindi: आम्रात मधुर, बृंहण, बलकारक, तर्पण, गुरु, स्नेहयुक्त, कफकारक, शीतल और वृष्य है; वह विष्टम्भ करके पचता है।
english: Āmrāta is sweet, nourishing, strengthening, replenishing (tarpaṇa), heavy, containing sneha (fat), Kapha-increasing, cold and aphrodisiac; it is digested after causing obstruction.
notes: āmrāta kept Sanskrit, no identification. jīryati: class-4 form of √jṝ, 'is digested'.
lines_deva: सस्नेहं श्लेष्मलं शीतं वृष्यं विष्टभ्य जीर्यति
lines_iast: sasnehaṃ śleṣmalaṃ śītaṃ vṛṣyaṃ viṣṭabhya jīryati

hindi: पकाए हुए ताल के शस्य और नारिकेल के फल बृंहण, स्निग्ध, शीतल, बलकारक और मधुर हैं।
english: Cooked tāla fruits (śasya) and nārikela fruits are nourishing, unctuous, cold, strengthening and sweet.
notes: śasya: crop, produce or fruit; 'fruit' is taken here (this is the group of fruits). siddhāni 'prepared, cooked' is read with tālaśasyāni; it could also cover both items. tāla = palmyra palm, nārikela = coconut (standard).

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: भव्य मधुर, अम्ल और कषाय, विष्टम्भी, गुरु, शीतल, पित्त और कफ को उत्पन्न करने वाला, ग्राही और मुख का शोधक है।
english: Bhavya is sweet, sour and astringent, obstructive, heavy and cold, produces Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman), is binding and cleanses the mouth.
notes: bhavya kept Sanskrit, no identification.

words.gram: n. nom. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: अम्ल परूषक, द्राक्षा, बदर और आरुक, तथा कर्कन्धु और निकुच भी पित्त और कफ को कुपित करते हैं।
english: Sour parūṣaka, drākṣā, badaras and ārukas, and also karkandhus and nikucas, aggravate Pitta and Kapha.
notes: amlam (n. sg.) agrees with parūṣakam; it may be meant for the whole list ('the sour ones'). drākṣā = grape, badara = jujube (standard); the others kept Sanskrit.

hindi: पूर्ण पका हुआ आरुक बहुत उष्ण नहीं, गुरु, प्रायः मधुर, मुख को प्रिय और बृंहण है; वह शीघ्र पचता है और दोषों को अधिक नहीं बढ़ाता।
english: Fully ripe āruka is not too hot, heavy, mostly sweet, pleasing to the mouth and nourishing; it is digested quickly and does not greatly increase the doṣas.
notes: āruka kept Sanskrit, no identification. guru 'heavy' stands beside 'digested quickly' as printed.

words.gloss: destroying aruci and excessive digestive fire
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: पारावत दो प्रकार का जानना चाहिए — शीत और उष्ण, तथा मधुर और अम्ल; वह गुरु है और अरुचि तथा अत्यग्नि का नाशक है।
english: Pārāvata should be known as of two kinds, cold and hot, and sweet and sour; it is heavy and destroys loss of taste (aruci) and excessive digestive fire (atyagni).
notes: The text names two kinds and two pairs of qualities without saying which quality goes with which kind. eva after amlam is a mere emphatic and is not rendered. pārāvata (here a fruit) kept Sanskrit, no identification.
lines_deva: द्विविधं शीतमुष्णं च मधुरं चाम्लमेव च
lines_iast: dvividhaṃ śītamuṣṇaṃ ca madhuraṃ cāmlameva ca

hindi: काश्मर्य का फल गुणों में भव्य से थोड़ा भिन्न कहा जाता है; ठीक वैसे ही अम्ल तूद गुणों में परूषक से थोड़ा भिन्न है।
english: The fruit of kāśmarya is said to differ little in qualities from bhavya; just so, sour tūda differs little in qualities from parūṣaka.
notes: kāśmarya and tūda kept Sanskrit, no identifications.

hindi: टङ्क कषाय-मधुर, वातकारक, गुरु और शीतल है। कच्चा कपित्थ कण्ठ के लिए हानिकारक, विषनाशक, ग्राही और वातकारक है।
english: Ṭaṅka is astringent and sweet, Vāta-increasing, heavy and cold. Unripe kapittha harms the throat, destroys poison, is binding and Vāta-increasing.
notes: kaṇṭhaghna is read literally, 'striking (harming) the throat'. kapittha = wood-apple (standard); ṭaṅka kept Sanskrit, no identification.

words.gloss: because of being sweet, sour and astringent

hindi: मधुर, अम्ल और कषाय होने से तथा सुगन्ध के कारण वह रुचि देने वाला है; और पूर्ण पका हुआ वह दोषनाशक, विषनाशक, ग्राही और गुरु भी है।
english: Because it is sweet, sour and astringent, and because of its fragrance, it gives relish; and when fully ripe it destroys the doṣas, destroys poison, is binding and also heavy.

text_flags.why: guru + api gives gurv api (u before a vowel becomes v); the printed guruvapi gives 9 syllables in the pāda, gurvapi the required 8 (vi ṣa ghnaṃ grā hi gur va pi: syllables 5-7 hi gur va = ⏑ – ⏑, as an even pāda requires)

notes: SENTENCE: the subject is kapittha of 136b; line a may describe the ripe fruit only.
lines_deva: परिपक्वं च दोषघ्नं विषघ्नं ग्राहि गुरुवपि
lines_iast: paripakvaṃ ca doṣaghnaṃ viṣaghnaṃ grāhi guruvapi

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: पका हुआ बिल्व तो दुर्जर, दोषकारक और दुर्गन्धित वायु उत्पन्न करने वाला है; वह कच्चा होने पर स्निग्ध, उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, दीपन और कफ-वात को जीतने वाला है।
english: Ripe bilva, however, is hard to digest, increases the doṣas and produces foul-smelling wind; when young it is unctuous, hot and sharp, stimulates digestion and overcomes Kapha and Vāta.
notes: vālam is the printed spelling of bālam 'young, unripe' (v/b alternation; 139 prints bālam), kept without a flag. pūtimāruta is a bahuvrīhi 'having (causing) foul wind'; māruta here is the physical wind (flatus), Hindi वायु. bilva = bael (standard).
lines_deva: बिल्वं तु दुर्जरं पक्वं दोषलं पूतिमारुतम्
lines_iast: bilvaṃ tu durjaraṃ pakvaṃ doṣalaṃ pūtimārutam

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: कच्चा (आम्र) रक्तपित्त उत्पन्न करता है, पूरा बढ़ा हुआ पित्त बढ़ाता है, और पका हुआ आम्र वायु को जीतता है तथा मांस, शुक्र और बल देता है।
english: Young (āmra) causes raktapitta, full-grown it increases Pitta; ripe āmra overcomes Vāta (vāyu) and gives flesh, semen and strength.
notes: āmra, named in line b, is taken as the subject of all three stages (young, full-grown, ripe). The optative jayet is rendered as a general statement. āmra = mango (standard).

words.gram: n. nom. sg., bahuvrīhi (dvandva first member)
n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: जाम्बव प्रायः कषाय और मधुर, गुरु, विष्टम्भी और शीतल है; वह कफ-पित्त का नाशक, ग्राही और अत्यधिक वातकारक है।
english: Jāmbava is mostly astringent and sweet, heavy, obstructive and cold; it destroys Kapha and Pitta, is binding and greatly productive of Vāta.

text_flags.why: possible: jāmbara is not a word; jāmbava (vṛddhi derivative of jambū, 'fruit of the jambū') fits this group of fruits (heading 125); jām ba raṃ and jām ba vaṃ have the same weights (– ⏑ –), so the metre does not decide

notes: The split and translations follow the suggested jāmbava; the printed jāmbaraṃ is kept in src. jāmbava kept Sanskrit.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: बदर मधुर, स्निग्ध, भेदन और वात-पित्त को जीतने वाला है; सूखा होने पर वह कफ-वात का नाशक है और पित्त में विरुद्ध नहीं होता।
english: Badara is sweet, unctuous, breaking (bhedana) and overcomes Vāta and Pitta; dried, it destroys Kapha and Vāta and is not incompatible in Pitta.
notes: badara = jujube (standard). virudhyate: class-4 ātmanepada, 'is opposed, conflicts'.
lines_deva: तच्छुष्कं कफवातघ्नं पित्ते न च विरुध्यते
lines_iast: tacchuṣkaṃ kaphavātaghnaṃ pitte na ca virudhyate

hindi: सिम्बितिका का फल कषाय-मधुर, शीतल और ग्राही है। गाङ्गेरुकी, करीर, बिम्बी, तोदन और धन्वन
english: The fruit of simbitikā is astringent and sweet, cold and binding. Gāṅgerukī, karīra, bimbī, todana and dhanvana
notes: The printed simbi(ñci)tikā carries the edition's bracketed alternative 'ñci' (its exact extent is not clear); the unbracketed simbitikā is used, and the bracket is left out of the translation (without it the line has 16 syllables). SENTENCE: the five names of line b take their qualities in 143a. todanadhanvanam is read as a samāhāra dvandva of two names. All names kept Sanskrit, no identifications.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: मधुर, कषाययुक्त, शीतल और पित्त-कफ को दूर करने वाले हैं। पूर्ण पका हुआ पनस, मोच और राजादन के फल
english: are sweet with astringency, cold, and remove Pitta and Kapha. Fully ripe panasa, moca and the fruits of rājādana
notes: SENTENCE: line a gives the qualities of the names in 142b (neuter singular for the group); line b runs into 144a. saṃpakva may go with panasa only or with all three. panasa = jackfruit, moca = banana (standard); rājādana kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: because of being astringent and non-slimy

hindi: मधुर, कषाययुक्त, स्निग्ध, शीतल और गुरु हैं। कषाय और विशद होने से तथा सुगन्ध के कारण रुचि देने वाला,
english: are sweet with astringency, unctuous, cold and heavy. Because of being astringent and non-slimy, and because of its fragrance, giving relish,
notes: SENTENCE: line a completes 143b; line b describes the lavalī fruit of 145a.

hindi: लवली का फल अवदंश के योग्य, हृद्य और वातकारक है। नीप, शताह्वक, पीलु, तृणशून्य, विकङ्कत
english: the fruit of lavalī is fit for an avadaṃśa (relish), cordial (hṛdya) and Vāta-increasing. Nīpa, śatāhvaka, pīlu, tṛṇaśūnya, vikaṅkata
notes: SENTENCE: line a takes the qualities of 144b; line b runs into 146a. avadaṃśa (something chewed as a relish) kept Sanskrit. Plant names kept Sanskrit and not split (tṛṇaśūnya, śatāhvaka as names), no identifications.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: और प्राचीनामलक — (ये) दोषनाशक और गर को हरने वाले हैं। ऐङ्गुद तिक्त-मधुर, स्निग्ध-उष्ण और कफ-वात को जीतने वाला है।
english: and prācīnāmalaka destroy the doṣas and remove gara (poison). Aiṅguda is bitter and sweet, unctuous and hot, and overcomes Kapha and Vāta.
notes: SENTENCE: line a completes the list of 145b (neuter singular for the group). eva after ca is not rendered. gara kept Sanskrit; aiṅguda kept Sanskrit, no identification.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
m. acc. pl., tat-puruṣa, ppp. caus. √vṛj

hindi: तिन्दुक कफ-पित्त का नाशक, कषाय, मधुर और लघु है। आमलक में लवण को छोड़कर सब रसों को जानना चाहिए;
english: Tinduka destroys Kapha and Pitta, and is astringent, sweet and light. In āmalaka one should know all the tastes except the salty;
notes: SENTENCE: line b runs into 148a (see there). tinduka kept Sanskrit, no identification.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: arising in rasa, blood, flesh and fat
words.gram: m. acc. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: वह रूक्ष, मधुर, कषाय और अम्ल है तथा कफ-पित्त को परम रूप से हरता है। बिभीतक रस, रक्त, मांस और मेद में उत्पन्न दोषों को नष्ट करता है,
english: it is dry, sweet, astringent and sour, and supremely removes Kapha and Pitta. Bibhītaka destroys the doṣas arising in rasa (body fluid), blood, flesh and fat,

text_flags.why: possible: asṛk + māṃsa gives asṛṅmāṃsa; 'gāṃsa' is no word, and māṃsa is printed in this chunk (139 māṃsaśukrabalapradam)

notes: SENTENCE: line a is read with āmalaka of 147b; grammatically (neuter singular) it could also describe bibhītaka of line b. Line b runs into 149a. bibhītaka kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: destroying hoarseness, moistness of Kapha and diseases of Pitta
words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: और स्वरभेद, कफ के उत्क्लेद और पित्त के रोगों का नाशक है। अम्ल, कषाय-मधुर, वातनाशक, ग्राही, दीपन,
english: and destroys hoarseness, the moistness (utkleda) of Kapha and the diseases of Pitta. Sour, astringent and sweet, Vāta-destroying, binding, stimulating digestion,
notes: SENTENCE: line a completes bibhītaka (148b); line b begins the qualities of dāḍima (150a). kaphotkleda may also be read as two items, Kapha and utkleda (moistness).

words.gloss: not incompatible with Kapha and Pitta
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: स्निग्ध और उष्ण दाडिम हृद्य है और कफ-पित्त का अविरोधी है। परन्तु जो दाडिम रूक्ष और अम्ल है, वह पित्त और अनिल को कुपित करता है।
english: unctuous and hot is dāḍima; it is cordial (hṛdya) and not incompatible with Kapha and Pitta. But the dāḍima that is dry and sour aggravates Pitta and Vāta (anila).
notes: SENTENCE: line a completes the qualities begun in 149b. dāḍima = pomegranate (standard).

hindi: मधुर (दाडिम) पित्त को दूर करता है; इनमें पहला दाडिम उत्तम है। बृक्षाम्ल ग्राही, रूक्ष और उष्ण है और वात-कफ में प्रशस्त है।
english: The sweet (dāḍima) removes Pitta; of these the former dāḍima is the best. Bṛkṣāmla is binding, dry and hot, and is recommended in Vāta-Kapha.
notes: pūrvam 'the former' is not specified further: it may be the first-described dāḍima (149b-150a) or the sweet one just named. bṛkṣāmla is the printed spelling of the name vṛkṣāmla (b/v alternation, as vālam/bālam in 138-139), kept without a flag; no identification.

hindi: पका हुआ अम्लिका का फल गुणों में उससे थोड़ा भिन्न है। अम्लवेतस उन्हीं गुणों से युक्त है, परन्तु भेदन है;
english: The ripe fruit of amlikā differs little from it in qualities. Amlavetasa, endowed with those same qualities, is however breaking (bhedana);
notes: tasmāt refers to bṛkṣāmla of 151b. SENTENCE: amlavetasa is the subject of the uses in 153-154a. amlikā and amlavetasa kept Sanskrit, no identifications.

hindi: शूल, अरुचि, विबन्ध, मन्द अग्नि, मद्य-विप्लव, हिक्का-श्वास, कास, वमन और मल के रोगों में —
english: in pain (śūla), loss of taste (aruci), obstruction (vibandha), weak digestive fire, the disorder of wine (madyaviplava), hiccup (hikkā) and dyspnoea, cough, vomiting and diseases of the faeces —
notes: SENTENCE: the uses of amlavetasa (152b), completed in 154a. hikkāśvāse is read as a samāhāra dvandva (n. loc. sg.), since hikkā alone would need a locative of its own.
lines_deva: हिक्काश्वासे च कासे च वम्यां वर्चोगदेषु च
lines_iast: hikkāśvāse ca kāse ca vamyāṃ varcogadeṣu ca

words.gram: m. loc. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: वात और कफ से उत्पन्न इन सभी में ही वह बताया जाता है। मातुलुङ्ग का केसर लघु है; शेष इससे भिन्न है।
english: in all of these arising from Vāta and Kapha it is indeed advised. The kesara (filaments) of mātuluṅga is light; the rest is otherwise than this.
notes: SENTENCE: line a completes 152b-153 (subject amlavetasa). kesara of mātuluṅga is rendered literally 'filaments'; 'the rest is otherwise' means the rest of the fruit is not light. mātuluṅga = citron (standard).

hindi: रुचिकारक, दीपन, हृद्य, सुगन्धित और छिलके से रहित — कर्चूर कफ-वात का नाशक तथा श्वास, हिक्का और अर्श के लिए हितकर है।
english: Giving relish, stimulating digestion, cordial (hṛdya), fragrant and freed of its skin, karcūra destroys Kapha and Vāta and is beneficial for dyspnoea, hiccup and arśas.
notes: The masculine adjectives of line a agree with karcūraḥ and are read with it; they could also continue mātuluṅga (m.) of 154b, and the text does not decide. karcūra kept Sanskrit, no identification; arśas kept Sanskrit.

hindi: नागरङ्ग का फल मधुर और थोड़ा अम्ल, हृद्य, भोजन में रुचि उत्पन्न करने वाला, दुर्जर, वातशामक और गुरु है।
english: The fruit of nāgaraṅga is sweet and slightly sour, cordial (hṛdya), gives relish for food, is hard to digest, pacifies Vāta and is heavy.
notes: nāgaraṅga = orange (standard).

words.gloss: vātama, abhiṣuka, akṣoṭa, mukūlaka and nikocaka

hindi: वातम, अभिषुक, अक्षोट, मुकूलक और निकोचक, उरुमाण सहित, गुरु, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, मधुर और बल देने वाले हैं;
english: Vātama, abhiṣuka, akṣoṭa, mukūlaka and nikocaka, together with urumāṇa, are heavy, hot, unctuous and sweet, and give strength;
notes: The first name is split as printed, vātama (short a before -mā-); a form vātāma would print vātāmā-; the metre allows either and the chunk gives no evidence, so no flag. SENTENCE: the qualities continue into 158a. All names kept Sanskrit, no identifications.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: वे वातनाशक, बृंहण, वृष्य और कफ-पित्त को बढ़ाने वाले हैं। प्रियाल को गुणों में इनके समान जानना चाहिए, उष्णता के बिना।
english: they destroy Vāta, are nourishing and aphrodisiac, and increase Kapha and Pitta. One should know priyāla to be similar to these in qualities, without the heat.
notes: SENTENCE: line a completes 157. auṣṇyaṃ vinā: priyāla shares their qualities except heat. priyāla kept Sanskrit, no identification.

hindi: श्लेष्मातक का फल कफकारक, मधुर, शीतल और गुरु है; अङ्कोट का फल कफकारक, गुरु, विष्टम्भी और अग्नि को जीतने वाला है।
english: The fruit of śleṣmātaka is Kapha-increasing (śleṣmala), sweet, cold and heavy; the fruit of aṅkoṭa is Kapha-increasing, heavy and obstructive, and overcomes the digestive fire (agni).

text_flags.why: the same word is printed viṣṭambhi in 128, 131, 136 and 140; the printed form lacks the vowel a and gives the half-line 15 syllables instead of 16

notes: agnijit is read literally, 'overcoming (the digestive) fire'. śleṣmātaka and aṅkoṭa kept Sanskrit, no identifications.
